chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: Dan Morgenstern and honest jazz writing
summary: Baker respects Morgenstern and Don DeMicheal as honest critics, and recalls Morgenstern supplying music for a Roy Eldridge commission overnight.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Dan Morgenstern, one of the major voices in jazz writing, one of the most honest people I’ve ever known. He along with Don DeMicheal, who died many years ago, were among the people that I respected most as writers, people that I knew could set aside their biases and write in an honest way, or at least state their biases up front, so you knew, when you were reading them, what those biases were before you started to read. And he’s somebody who I think is a great scholar. I can remember calling him when I got ready to write a piece which was commissioned for Roy Eldridge two years before he died. I couldn’t find some of the music. I called him on the phone that morning. The next morning I had the music that I needed to start, I had the recording that I needed to work from.
